6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: The administration had been working day and night on the overwhelming amount of issues that were facing the country.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: After I'd signed dozens of them, I closed my eyes to relax for a moment.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: On top of all that, I'd finally managed to set up a meeting with the Old Guards to talk about a path of no reforms and cooperation. It was in thirty minutes.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Even though I couldn't wait to leave the Palace for the day, Lucian had earlier told me that the Chief Justice wanted to speak to me. We were to meet in my office in thirty minutes.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: Thousands of shimmering lights in the Holsord skyline were mesmerising.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: It eased my mind a little.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: I was either going to cooperate with them, or would have no choice but to work with the reformists on the new Constitution.

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: I waited for him, wondering what he wanted to talk about.

25.speaker: Lucian Galade
25.text: "The Chief Justice insisted on seeing you this evening. I do not know what he has to say but it will probably be about the new Constitution."

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: Suddenly, I heard a knock on the door.

28.speaker: Lucian Galade
28.text: "Soon, Mr. Hawker will be coming to the meeting with Mr. Garaci."

29.speaker: Lucian Galade
29.text: "Before they come, we should talk about our strategy, sir."

30.speaker: Lucian Galade
30.text: "I'm sorry that I couldn't explain the situation to you in detail earlier, sir."

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: He sat on a chair near my desk.

36.speaker: Lucian Galade
36.text: "He will be coming shortly with Judge Garaci to the meeting. We shouldn't take them lightly."

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “They are here to threaten us to stop the reforms.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “I think he's here to test the waters."

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “We may be able to cooperate with them.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “Regardless of what they say, I will continue with the new Constitution.”

41.speaker: Player
41.text: “I knew they would come. We all want the same thing.”

42.speaker: Lucian Galade
42.text: "I agree. They will probably try to get you to their side."

43.speaker: Lucian Galade
43.text: "We knew they would react at some point."

44.speaker: Lucian Galade
44.text: "I advise against that, sir. I do not trust the Chief Justice."

45.speaker: Lucian Galade
45.text: "Of course. Let's stand our ground and not let them antagonize us, sir."

46.speaker: Lucian Galade
46.text: "I'm sure they have heard about your intentions regarding the reforms. They must be coming here to make a deal."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: Livia opened the doors. Chief Justice Orso Hawker and Judge Heron Garaci entered the room.

49.speaker: Narrator
49.text: There were three knocks at the door.

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: Lucian checked his watch. He looked rather worried.

51.speaker: Orso Hawker
51.text: "Good evening, Mr. President. It's great to see you."

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “There is nothing to talk about. Let's see what they have to say."

55.speaker: Player
55.text: “I aim to get a deal out of this meeting."

56.speaker: Lucian Galade
56.text: "We should be careful when dealing with the Old Guard, sir."

57.speaker: Lucian Galade
57.text: "We should try not to antagonize them. In case we don't collaborate with them, we'll need their support in the Court's vote."

58.speaker: Lucian Galade
58.text: "And... I know I told you this before, sir. But I wouldn't trust the Chief Justice."

59.speaker: Lucian Galade
59.text: "We should be careful when dealing with the Old Guard, sir."

61.speaker: Player
61.text: “Duly noted, Lucian. I'll see about that myself."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “I've heard this enough, Lucian. I told you my intentions."

64.speaker: Lucian Galade
64.text: "Glad we're on the same page, sir."

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: He sat on a chair near my desk.

76.speaker: Lucian Galade
76.text: "No thank you, sir. But good to see you enjoying yourself."

78.speaker: Player
78.text: “Welcome, Justice Garaci and Chief Justice Hawker."

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: Orso gestured at the sofa in the office.

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: He gave me a blank stare and readjusted himself on the sofa.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: We all took our seats on two opposite sofas and made ourselves comfortable.

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: Orso glanced at the glass of whiskey.

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “Forgive me, would you also like to have a drink?"

93.speaker: Heron Garaci
93.text: "How were your first couple of months, Mr. President? I hope you're faring well."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "I don't think that's relevant to our meeting, Mr. Hawker."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "Can we get to the point, Mr. Hawker?"

98.speaker: Orso Hawker
98.text: “I'd like to stay as conscious and focused as I can."

100.speaker: Orso Hawker
100.text: “A man needs his drink, I understand."

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: The various government departments were sending me an avalanche of documents, all of which required my signature so they could start working on the new plans that had been decided on.

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "Thank you, it's very busy but I'm doing good."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "To be honest, it was a rough start."

107.speaker: Player
107.text: "I'm doing well. No need to worry, Mr. Garaci."

108.speaker: Player
108.text: "No need for pleasantries. Let's just get to the point."

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: They both gave me blank stares. Orso readjusted himself on the sofa.

112.speaker: Heron Garaci
112.text: "That's great to hear, Mr. President. We also think you've been doing a good job so far."

113.speaker: Heron Garaci
113.text: "I couldn't imagine. Yet, I think you're doing a good job so far."

114.speaker: Heron Garaci
114.text: "Considering all that's happening around us. With the shootings near the Palace and soldiers on our borders..."

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: He let out a deep sigh.

117.speaker: Heron Garaci
117.text: "It will only get busier. Yet, I think you're doing a good job so far."

118.speaker: Orso Hawker
118.text: “You invited us here this evening to talk about a possible cooperation."

119.speaker: Orso Hawker
119.text: “So, let us hear it from you. What do you have in mind, Mr. President?"

122.speaker: Orso Hawker
122.text: "You probably know why we are here."

124.speaker: Orso Hawker
124.text: "We've heard that you're not giving full support to the reforms."

126.speaker: Player
126.text: "You must have heard wrong, Mr. Hawker."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "You're here to stop the new Constitution."

132.speaker: Player
132.text: "I want to protect the current Constitution."

135.speaker: Player
135.text: "We need to stay united in times of possible conflict."

136.speaker: Orso Hawker
136.text: "That's relieving to hear. Sordland has plunged into chaos because of them."

137.speaker: Orso Hawker
137.text: "Looks like we are on the same page."

138.speaker: Orso Hawker
138.text: "I agree. Sordland is in a dire situation right now. We need to stay focused on our real problems."

140.speaker: Orso Hawker
140.text: "Looks like we are on the same page."

141.speaker: Orso Hawker
141.text: "The question is not where I heard that, but if it's true or not."

143.speaker: Orso Hawker
143.text: "So, you are going to push to change the Constitution, after all?"

144.speaker: Orso Hawker
144.text: "We would be honored to work together."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "No, I'd rather work with you, if that's a possibility."

149.speaker: Player
149.text: "It's neither true or false, I'm weighing my options first."

151.speaker: Orso Hawker
151.text: "We are only here to tell you that the Supreme Court does not approve of the attempt to change the Constitution."

152.speaker: Orso Hawker
152.text: "We know you are working on a new Constitution."

153.speaker: Orso Hawker
153.text: "The Supreme Court does not approve of this."

154.speaker: Lucian Galade
154.text: "With all due respect, the Constitution needs to be updated, sir. I am sure you are well aware of the public demand and our circumstances."

159.speaker: Orso Hawker
159.text: "Is that so? I see that you are the one who is not aware of our actual circumstances."

160.speaker: Orso Hawker
160.text: "And the public demanded to give more powers to the President? Spare me the lecture, I know you have *different* ideas."

161.speaker: Orso Hawker
161.text: "Having said that, there are some things you need to be aware of."

162.speaker: Heron Garaci
162.text: "Yes, Mr. President. Our national values and sovereignty are under attack. We must be vigilant and aggressive against these reformists. It's clear that their reforms are a conspiracy of foreign powers."

164.speaker: Player
164.text: "I've read the security reports. I am suspecting something big too."

166.speaker: Orso Hawker
166.text: "In any case, it would have been an honor to work together."

167.speaker: Orso Hawker
167.text: "Even if your proposal passes the Assembly, I will make sure it will not pass the Supreme Court. That much is clear."

168.speaker: Orso Hawker
168.text: "You want to make a weaker Constitution in the midst of problems from both inside and outside."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "You haven't even seen the proposal yet, Mr. Hawker. Isn't it too soon to be against it?"

170.speaker: Player
170.text: "So you came here to threaten us."

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "Come on, Mr. Hawker. We can figure something out."

172.speaker: Heron Garaci
172.text: "Mr. President, if you are not aware of these plots, you should really reconsider your team of advisers."

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "We'll get the Court too, even if you do not cooperate."

174.speaker: Orso Hawker
174.text: "Do you think I live under a rock, Mr. President?"

176.speaker: Orso Hawker
176.text: "How was that a threat, Mr. President? I merely stated my position."

177.speaker: Heron Garaci
177.text: "There is no threat here, Mr. President."

179.speaker: Orso Hawker
179.text: "If you decide to give us a listen."

181.speaker: Orso Hawker
181.text: "Justices of the Supreme Court cannot be bought."

183.speaker: Heron Garaci
183.text: "Yet you, Mr. President, seem to be only partially informed about the current situation. Please let us explain the reasons of our stance."

184.speaker: Heron Garaci
184.text: "Mr. President, you seem to be only partially informed about the current situation. Please let us explain the reasons of our stance."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "I believe I am fully informed about the situation, Mr. Garaci."

189.speaker: Lucian Galade
189.text: "With all due respect, how could a Justice have better security intel than the President of Sordland?"

191.speaker: Heron Garaci
191.text: "It's not only some *thing*, Mr. President. The superpowers are playing chess in Sordland."

192.speaker: Heron Garaci
192.text: "Mr. President, if you are not aware of these plots, you should really reconsider your team of advisers."

193.speaker: Orso Hawker
193.text: "Please let me explain. We have important information you may not have heard yet."

194.speaker: Orso Hawker
194.text: "That is a good question. How? Maybe you should first see if your security team is worth trusting."

196.speaker: Player
196.text: "I trust my team, Mr. Hawker. You shouldn't concern yourself with these matters."

198.speaker: Orso Hawker
198.text: "I did not want to offend you, Mr. President. But I meant it."

199.speaker: Orso Hawker
199.text: "I have incriminating evidence against a very prominent political personality."

200.speaker: Orso Hawker
200.text: "But before I give you that... I've had a couple of questions on my mind."

201.speaker: Heron Garaci
201.text: "Sordland has more important problems and threats that we should face right now instead of nitpicking about some paragraphs of the Constitution. We have a potential war within our borders."

202.speaker: Heron Garaci
202.text: "We are protecting the Constitution, because it works, Mr. President. It is efficient and it gives you the authority to lead the nation with swift decisions."

203.speaker: Heron Garaci
203.text: "That's exactly what they want you to say."

204.speaker: Heron Garaci
204.text: "You think you are, Mr. President. But the Chief Justice has some intel on something that you would be very interested in."

208.speaker: Orso Hawker
208.text: "Mr. President. I know that you are a busy man, so I will make this quick."

209.speaker: Narrator
209.text: Orso signalled Heron with his hand to let him speak instead.

212.speaker: Player
212.text: "I am not interested in your games."

213.speaker: Orso Hawker
213.text: "What do you think about the offensive posturing of Rumburg and their KA-74's being found in the hands of the Blud separatists?"

214.speaker: Player
214.text: "I am very troubled by that. We need to be prepared against Rumburg."

215.speaker: Player
215.text: "Blud separatists must be dealt with before they gain the support of the Bluds."

216.speaker: Player
216.text: "The connection is not that strong, I don't think they are a real threat."

217.speaker: Orso Hawker
217.text: "Is the administration doing something about that?"

218.speaker: Orso Hawker
218.text: "We all know what the Bludish Freedom Front stands for. How come stashes of Rumburgian KA rifles do not trouble you?"

219.speaker: Player
219.text: "I don't think the organization is strong enough to create problems."

220.speaker: Player
220.text: "We haven't found thousands of it. That is not enough to establish a direct connection."

221.speaker: Player
221.text: "My security team is working on that."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "We are not rushing with our actions just yet."

223.speaker: Player
223.text: "Not as fast as I'd like to."

228.speaker: Orso Hawker
228.text: "And you said you will not focus on military during your term. How is that for a preparation? You will be the one to blame if you actually proceed with that campaign talk."

230.speaker: Heron Garaci
230.text: "We hope that regardless of your promise, you increase the security measures and put every Sord's mind at a little more ease."

234.speaker: Orso Hawker
234.text: "Have you even talked with your own generals? Or Mr. Lancea? I don't think they share your views, Mr. President."

235.speaker: Orso Hawker
235.text: "And you said you will not focus on military during your term. Are you aware what that could mean for Sordland? You will be the one to blame if you actually proceed with that campaign talk."

236.speaker: Orso Hawker
236.text: "We need an increase on our security budgets. This is an actual emergency. It affects all of Sordland."

240.speaker: Orso Hawker
240.text: "Sure, Mr. President. It is a demand. A just and logical one."

242.speaker: Orso Hawker
242.text: "Are you also aware that the armed Bludish separatists have direct connections with the Workers Party of Bludia?"

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "The Worker's Party is a democratic party unlike the militias. They are not the same."

247.speaker: Orso Hawker
247.text: "They may claim they have no ties with the separatists, but most of their members used to be part of them before they formed the Workers Party of Bludia."

248.speaker: Heron Garaci
248.text: "How about the name, Mr. President? It is not the 'Workers Party of Sordland', is it? As far as I am aware, there is no nation called Bludia around here."

249.speaker: Heron Garaci
249.text: "They are. And both organizations want the same thing. To gain independence from Sordland."

250.speaker: Orso Hawker
250.text: "You know what that means. Do you remember the vote of the Workers'Party in the last election?"

252.speaker: Orso Hawker
252.text: "Today, the only reason they are not in the Assembly is because of the electoral threshold. They have gotten quite big too. They are clearly getting outside help and their connections to the paramilitary Bludish force cannot be denied."

253.speaker: Orso Hawker
253.text: "And all of a sudden, the reformists are trying to decrease the electoral threshold, so that the Bludish separatists can be legitimized in the Assembly to achieve their aims of independence."

255.speaker: Player
255.text: "That's why we cannot allow it, Mr. Hawker."

257.speaker: Orso Hawker
257.text: "Say what you will, Mr. President. I am stating the obvious."

260.speaker: Orso Hawker
260.text: "I wish the only issues were the Bludish terrorists and Rumburg."

261.speaker: Orso Hawker
261.text: "Now we have conflicts on the streets between the nationalists and the communists. And the communists are gathering really fast after the shooting of Circas."

262.speaker: Orso Hawker
262.text: "This could potentially lead to civil war, Mr. President. We know that United Contana supports the communists in Sordland."

263.speaker: Player
263.text: "What does that have to do with anything?"

264.speaker: Player
264.text: "With all due respect, that does not really concern you."

266.speaker: Orso Hawker
266.text: "We all know that Sordish security forces found stashes of Rumburgian weaponry in the hideouts of Bludish separatists. KA-74's are roaming inside Sordland at this moment."

267.speaker: Orso Hawker
267.text: "As much as Rumburg poses a direct threat, now it's clear that they are also intervening in our country and weaponising our minorities against us. It's not unprecedented to think that the Bluds will start their terror again with their new toys."

268.speaker: Orso Hawker
268.text: "Not to mention the fights that broke out between the left and right wing after the shooting of Bernard Circas. Communists are rising with the support of United Contana. The chaos is imminent for Sordland."

272.speaker: Orso Hawker
272.text: "And sadly we don't see the administration taking the necessary precautions. You said you will not focus on military during your term. Under current circumstances that cannot be tolerated at any cost."

273.speaker: Orso Hawker
273.text: "And sadly we don't see the administration taking the necessary precautions yet. We clearly need more funding for our security forces for the days to come."

274.speaker: Player
274.text: "Mr. Hawker, the Court has no jurisdiction over these matters."

275.speaker: Player
275.text: "We are taking the necessary steps. No need to worry."

276.speaker: Player
276.text: "I did promise that but the circumstances have changed."

277.speaker: Player
277.text: "Tolerate!? You should be more careful with your words of choice."

278.speaker: Player
278.text: "Mr. Hawker, the Court has no jurisdiction over these matters."

279.speaker: Player
279.text: "We are taking the necessary steps, no need to worry."

280.speaker: Player
280.text: "I will actually be increasing the security budget shortly."

281.speaker: Orso Hawker
281.text: "Aren't we all part of this State, Mr. President? We are all responsible if Sordland fails to overcome these threats."

282.speaker: Orso Hawker
282.text: "We hope that our police forces and our military is adequately funded during these times of conflict."

284.speaker: Orso Hawker
284.text: "Surely a decision to destroy Sordland cannot be tolerated whether it comes from you or President Soll. Why can't you admit that we are making sense here?"

285.speaker: Orso Hawker
285.text: "Aren't we all part of this State, Mr. President? We are all responsible if Sordland fails to overcome these threats."

286.speaker: Orso Hawker
286.text: "We hope that our police forces and our military is adequately funded during these times of conflict."

288.speaker: Orso Hawker
288.text: "But regardless of that, are you also aware that the armed Bludish separatists have direct connections with the Worker's Party of Bludia?"

292.speaker: Player
292.text: "The Worker's Party is a democratic party unlike the militias. They are not the same."

293.speaker: Orso Hawker
293.text: "They may claim they have no ties with the separatists, but most of their members used to be part of them before they formed the Workers' Party of Bludia."

294.speaker: Heron Garaci
294.text: "They are. And both organizations want the same thing. To gain independence from Sordland."

295.speaker: Heron Garaci
295.text: "How about the name, Mr. President? It is not the 'Workers' Party of Sordland', is it? As far as I am aware, there is no nation called Bludia around here."

296.speaker: Orso Hawker
296.text: "You know what that means. Do you remember the vote of the Workers' Party in the last election?"

298.speaker: Orso Hawker
298.text: "The only reason they are not in the Assembly is because of the electoral threshold. They have gotten quite big. They are clearly getting outside help and their connections to the paramilitary Bludish force cannot be denied."

299.speaker: Orso Hawker
299.text: "And all of a sudden, the reformists are trying to decrease the electoral threshold, so that the Bludish separatists can be legitimized in the Assembly to achieve their aims of independence."

301.speaker: Player
301.text: "I will not allow it to happen."

303.speaker: Orso Hawker
303.text: "Say what you will, Mr. President. I am stating the obvious."

305.speaker: Orso Hawker
305.text: "But I wish the only issues were the Bludish terrorists and Rumburg."

307.speaker: Heron Garaci
307.text: "The Reformists' suggested changes would also bring the communists -- who are backed by United Contana -- into the Assembly. Do you see the pattern yet?"

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "You're saying the reformists are working for the foreign powers?"

309.speaker: Player
309.text: "I apologise, gentlemen. But I am not a conspiracy theorist."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "There is no evidence about any of this."

312.speaker: Player
312.text: "I am not working with the reformists, Mr. Hawker."

316.speaker: Orso Hawker
316.text: "I am aware. Yet you're proceeding with your own version of changes to the Constitution, aren't you?"

317.speaker: Player
317.text: "I am. The new Constitution will not be weaker but stronger."

319.speaker: Player
319.text: "Yes. I need more powers to fix these problems."

320.speaker: Player
320.text: "Unless you have something better to propose."

321.speaker: Orso Hawker
321.text: "You already have the power of the decrees, Mr. President. As long as we work together, we can allow you to enact major changes with the presidential decrees."

322.speaker: Heron Garaci
322.text: "This is not a conspiracy theory. Haven't you been briefed by your security team? Maybe you should suspect them as well."

323.speaker: Heron Garaci
323.text: "Haven't you been briefed by your security team? Maybe you should suspect them as well."

324.speaker: Orso Hawker
324.text: "We should take the necessary measures against communist and Bludish plots as well as increasing our military budget against a possible conflict with Rumburg."

325.speaker: Heron Garaci
325.text: "And of course not fall into the traps of the reformists by listening to their demands. They are clearly plotting to weaken the President and our whole administration in order to exploit the situation."

326.speaker: Orso Hawker
326.text: "...Which brings us to some very important information that we have. It's definitely something you need to hear, and it can change absolutely everything."

327.speaker: Lucian Galade
327.text: "With all due respect, Mr. President, I think this is getting slightly ridiculous."

329.speaker: Player
329.text: "You're right. I don't think anything will come out of this meeting."

332.speaker: Orso Hawker
332.text: "So you don't want to hear about the information that I have?"

333.speaker: Orso Hawker
333.text: "The person in question is Mr. Frens Ricter, himself. The *leader* of the reformists."

334.speaker: Orso Hawker
334.text: "We have enough information to infer that he has ties with Arcasia."

335.speaker: Orso Hawker
335.text: "Arcasia is aggressively growing their influence around the world and now we have Mr. Ricter coming up with these ridiculous demands for a new Constitution amidst a chaotic period in Sordland."

336.speaker: Lucian Galade
336.text: "How would you know that Mr. Ricter has ties to Arcasia?"

337.speaker: Orso Hawker
337.text: "All the pieces seem to fit perfectly. That is why the Supreme Court will be doing what it takes to stop these reforms and preserve the Constitution."

338.speaker: Orso Hawker
338.text: "He was spotted in a hotel in Arcasia last year, where they held the 'Conference on Economic Development in Volatile Regions'. Right around that time, he started to influence the masses into believing that our Constitution is the reason for everything bad."

339.speaker: Heron Garaci
339.text: "Mr. Galade, we all know he has been in Arcasia many times, because it's been documented. But what would you think if I told you he has been making hidden flights to the country?"

340.speaker: Player
340.text: "I need to know this. Please explain."

341.speaker: Player
341.text: "He was hiding his flights to Arcasia?"

344.speaker: Orso Hawker
344.text: "His trip was not documented, nor was he an official guest of the conference. We believe that he had a meeting with President Walker behind closed doors."

345.speaker: Orso Hawker
345.text: "I also have more photos of him that were taken in Arcasia in different cities. One is from a couple months back. Again, none of it is documented."

346.speaker: Orso Hawker
346.text: "He also attended another event in Lespia last week. The Arcasian Minister of Foreign Affairs was there too."

347.speaker: Player
347.text: "How did you find out about this?"

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "How can any of these be undocumented?"

350.speaker: Orso Hawker
350.text: "We don't know. Even if he used a private plane, we would be able to get the information of his flights. That means he has people helping them from inside."

351.speaker: Orso Hawker
351.text: "Many Sollists were already following his leads for quite some time, Mr. President. I cannot give away their identities, but I can give you the evidence."

352.speaker: Narrator
352.text: He handed me a small file.

354.speaker: Narrator
354.text: It contained official documents from the Sordish Border Guard with highlighted dates that showed no trace of Frens Ricter's name.

355.speaker: Narrator
355.text: There were clear photos of him that were taken in the conference in Arcasia, as well as remarks by Lespian and Arcasian citizens who claim to have seen him with Arcasian businessmen around the same dates.

356.speaker: Narrator
356.text: There was also an official transcript of one of his speeches where he claimed to be in Benfi on the dates of the conference in Arcasia, where he was spotted.

358.speaker: Orso Hawker
358.text: "Of course they are real, Mr. Galade."

359.speaker: Orso Hawker
359.text: "Believe what you will, Mr. President. But at least hear me out."

360.speaker: Orso Hawker
360.text: "Now you understand the reasons for our current stance. And also our suspicions about your advisers, who clearly have not given you this vital information."

361.speaker: Narrator
361.text: Lucian gave him a sharp look.

362.speaker: Player
362.text: "There is no need, Mr. Hawker. This meeting is over."

366.speaker: Narrator
366.text: Lucian skimmed through the documents with skepticism which slowly turned into surprise.

367.speaker: Orso Hawker
367.text: "We should take the necessary measures against communist and Bludish plots as well as increasing our military budget against a possible conflict with Rumburg."

368.speaker: Heron Garaci
368.text: "The Reformists' suggested changes would also bring the communists -- who are backed by United Contana -- into the Assembly. Do you see the pattern yet?"

369.speaker: Player
369.text: "You're saying the reformists are working for the foreign powers?"

371.speaker: Player
371.text: "I apologize gentlemen but I am not a conspiracy theorist."

373.speaker: Heron Garaci
373.text: "Haven't you been briefed by your security team? Maybe you should start suspecting them too."

374.speaker: Heron Garaci
374.text: "This is not a conspiracy theory. Haven't you been briefed by your security team? Maybe you should start suspecting them too."

376.speaker: Heron Garaci
376.text: "And of course not fall into the traps of the reformists by listening to their demands. They are clearly plotting to weaken the President and our whole administration in order to exploit the situation."

377.speaker: Orso Hawker
377.text: "...Which brings us to the information that I have about this important figure."

380.speaker: Orso Hawker
380.text: "The person in question is Mr. Frens Ricter, himself."

381.speaker: Orso Hawker
381.text: "We have enough information to infer that he has ties with Arcasia."

382.speaker: Orso Hawker
382.text: "All the pieces seem to fit perfectly. That is why the Supreme Court will be doing what it takes to stop these reforms and preserve the Constitution together with you."

383.speaker: Orso Hawker
383.text: "Arcasia is aggressively growing their influence around the world and now we have Mr. Ricter coming up with these ridiculous demands for a new Constitution amidst a chaotic period in Sordland."

384.speaker: Lucian Galade
384.text: "How would you know that Mr. Ricter has ties to Arcasia?"

385.speaker: Orso Hawker
385.text: "...At least that's what we hope for."

386.speaker: Orso Hawker
386.text: "There is not much to think or check... This is clearly an emergency. In such cases, the Constitution gives the President the right to use his emergency powers. If we work together, you can be sure that the Supreme Court will not block your declaration of emergency."

387.speaker: Lucian Galade
387.text: "We appreciate the information, Mr. Hawker, but I advise against jumping to conclusions right away. We still need to check the information."

388.speaker: Player
388.text: "Let's talk about how we can work together."

389.speaker: Player
389.text: "You want me to declare an emergency?"

390.speaker: Player
390.text: "I am still too skeptical about these, Mr. Hawker. I will have to decline."

391.speaker: Lucian Galade
391.text: "What is that supposed to mean, Mr. Hawker?"

392.speaker: Orso Hawker
392.text: "It seems you are more influenced by Mr. Galade than you think."

393.speaker: Orso Hawker
393.text: "Of course. We cannot wait for the processes of the Assembly to take care of these issues. You must exercise your presidential powers for a fast and effective solution."

394.speaker: Orso Hawker
394.text: "Which means you might need to suspend parts of the Constitution to give more authority to our security forces to deal with these issues. We must officially investigate Mr. Ricter as well."

395.speaker: Orso Hawker
395.text: "You can devise a strong security decree if you can base it on the Articles 57 and 58, which gives the president the right to suspend parts of the Constitution to deal with national security threats."

396.speaker: Orso Hawker
396.text: "You can directly bypass the Assembly in such a situation. The only thing you need is the Supreme Court to allow the emergency to be declared. And you have our word on that."

397.speaker: Lucian Galade
397.text: "Sir, I think that is going a bit too far. We shouldn't escalate things so fast."

398.speaker: Orso Hawker
398.text: "We can devise a plan together. I know how we can use the Constitution to our advantage. It would be more effective if Mr. Galade and Mr. Garaci leave the room before we discuss it."

400.speaker: Player
400.text: "Could you leave us alone with Mr. Hawker, gentlemen?"

404.speaker: Narrator
404.text: Lucian looked at me to hear my response.

405.speaker: Player
405.text: "I like your idea, Mr. Hawker but I'd rather plan it together."

406.speaker: Player
406.text: "I'm sorry to say that we won't be cooperating, Mr. Hawker."

407.speaker: Player
407.text: "Regardless of our situation, I'll be proceeding with the reforms."

408.speaker: Orso Hawker
408.text: "Even though you are aware of our national security threats..."

409.speaker: Heron Garaci
409.text: "You are making a big mistake, Mr. President. We will not allow you to succeed."

410.speaker: Orso Hawker
410.text: "Why don't you explain your agenda yourself, Lucian? You are swaying the President to ignore the national security threats."

411.speaker: Player
411.text: "I am not swayed by anyone, Mr. Hawker. This is my own decision."

412.speaker: Player
412.text: "You are the one trying to sway me into believing in conspiracies."

413.speaker: Orso Hawker
413.text: "Say what you will. History will prove us right, once again."

414.speaker: Heron Garaci
414.text: "And if you believe you can enact these reforms, you are living in a land of dreams."

416.speaker: Narrator
416.text: There was a long silence in the room.

417.speaker: Orso Hawker
417.text: "It seems the President is done with us, Heron. Let's take our leave."

419.speaker: Orso Hawker
419.text: "Well, Mr. President. Do you want to talk about how we can fight against these reformists and the others? Or did you made up your mind?"

421.speaker: Player
421.text: "No, Mr. Hawker. I think this meeting is over."

422.speaker: Orso Hawker
422.text: "Mr. President, why don't we talk in private, just the two of us?"

423.speaker: Player
423.text: "You are the ones who are making the mistake."

424.speaker: Player
424.text: "Gentlemen, I think it's about time to end this meeting."

425.speaker: Orso Hawker
425.text: "Well, thank you for having us, Mr. President."

426.speaker: Orso Hawker
426.text: "We will see, Mr. President. We will see..."

429.speaker: Orso Hawker
429.text: "Glad to hear that we're on the same page, Mr. President. But I will have to insist on the private talk."

430.speaker: Player
430.text: "Fair enough. Will you leave us, gentlemen?"

432.speaker: Lucian Galade
432.text: "You know exactly what I think. But if you both insist upon it, I will leave."

434.speaker: Narrator
434.text: Lucian stood up as Orso gave him a smile. Heron paid his respects and left with Lucian, leaving me and Orso alone.

436.speaker: Orso Hawker
436.text: "If you stop the reform committee meetings immediately and focus on the real threats, I will guarantee you, we will manage the reformists together."

437.speaker: Orso Hawker
437.text: "You must eliminate these threats both internal and external. An emergency act can help you do that. We cannot trust anyone in the administration either."

438.speaker: Player
438.text: "Tell me more about the legal details of an emergency act."

439.speaker: Player
439.text: "How can we fight against these threats with an emergency act?"

440.speaker: Orso Hawker
440.text: "According to Article 58, if public security and order are seriously disturbed or endangered within the Republic of Sordland..."

441.speaker: Orso Hawker
441.text: "...the President of Sordland may modify and suspend parts of Constitution, subject to confirmation by the Supreme Court, to determine the validity of the declaration of a state of emergency."

442.speaker: Player
442.text: "Which parts of the Constitution can we modify or suspend?"

443.speaker: Player
443.text: "How can we effectively silence the opposition?"

445.speaker: Orso Hawker
445.text: "That is kind of a grey area. The Constitution states that..."

446.speaker: Player
446.text: "I agree. Sordland is in a crisis."

448.speaker: Orso Hawker
448.text: "...no State shall, in the case of National Emergency, modify or suspend the rights of freedom, defined in Article 100 of the Constitution, unless actually invaded, or in such imminent danger as will not admit of delay."

449.speaker: Player
449.text: "If we want to give the police more authority, we might need to modify the rights of freedom too."

450.speaker: Player
450.text: "Such imminent danger... That can definitely be argued to be the case."

451.speaker: Orso Hawker
451.text: "That is correct. Current security laws are limited because of the personal freedoms defined in Article 100. We may need to suspend some of the privacy laws which definitely conflicts with the Constitution..."

453.speaker: Orso Hawker
453.text: "However, the section where it states that 'actually invaded, or in such imminent danger as will not admit of delay' can be up to interpretation. We are definitely under such imminent danger because of Rumburg."

454.speaker: Orso Hawker
454.text: "Not to mention United Contana's support for a communist coup in Sordland as well as Frens Ricter's involvement with Arcasia, which is definitely connected to all of these problems."

457.speaker: Orso Hawker
457.text: "It can definitely be argued that we are under such imminent danger because of Rumburg."

458.speaker: Orso Hawker
458.text: "And of course, that is up to the Supreme Court to decide. So that is not a problem."

459.speaker: Orso Hawker
459.text: "You have the power to give more authority to the police with their search warrants, suspicion- based arrests, detention without trials... as well as banning the threatening nations' citizens from entering Sordland."

460.speaker: Orso Hawker
460.text: "We may need increased surveillance on our political rivals to find out about their connections and plots. Bringing unlimited detention would allow you to arrest people as necessary, such as Mr. Ricter."

461.speaker: Player
461.text: "What if the investigations cannot find anything incriminating?"

463.speaker: Player
463.text: "That might be going a bit too far."

464.speaker: Orso Hawker
464.text: "I disagree. You already know about the coup plots and foreign backed terrorists in Sordland. And a lot of these issues overlap with the reformist agenda of creating a weaker Constitution."

465.speaker: Orso Hawker
465.text: "I suspect Frens Ricter is involved with many of these organisations. He may even be working together with Rumburg. And they really do pose an existential threat to Sordland."

466.speaker: Orso Hawker
466.text: "The information that I gave you can be enough, depending on what parts of the Constitution you'll modify. In an emergency, anything is possible, Mr. President."

467.speaker: Orso Hawker
467.text: "The Supreme Court will support your decisions."

468.speaker: Orso Hawker
468.text: "I agree. In an emergency, anything is possible, Mr. President..."

469.speaker: Orso Hawker
469.text: "According to the Constitution, only the President and the Grand National Assembly can revoke the emergency after it is declared. That is correct."

470.speaker: Orso Hawker
470.text: "However, as long as your party is in line, they will never have a majority to revoke it immediately. So, no. They cannot *simply* revoke it."

481.speaker: Player
481.text: "Let's talk about the details of this emergency act."

482.speaker: Orso Hawker
482.text: "You must first justify the emergency act. We need to have at least one target that we can blame the conflicts on. They will be declared as a national security threat, and this would allow us to prosecute their members or people connected to them."

483.speaker: Player
483.text: "Young Sords executed an attack near the Palace. They must pay for it."

484.speaker: Player
484.text: "Red Youth must be targeted before they get too powerful to trigger a revolution."

485.speaker: Orso Hawker
485.text: "These seem to suggest that Arcasia is behind the reformists. Their demands will only benefit Arcasia. They want us to have a weaker administration while we face all these threats."

486.speaker: Orso Hawker
486.text: "This is clearly a plot against Sordland. I bet Rumburg is part of their plan too. It cannot be a coincidence that they are weaponizing our minorities against us around the same time."

487.speaker: Player
487.text: "Gentlemen, let's get back to the topic."

500.speaker: Orso Hawker
500.text: "There are obvious connections between the Bludish separatists and Rumburg. And the separatists have clear connections to the Worker's Party of Bludia. They should be declared a national security threat and the party should be banned."

501.speaker: Orso Hawker
501.text: "Red Youth must also be our target. They are plotting a communist revolution in Sordland with clear funding from United Contana. And now they took to the streets after the death of Bernard Circas. There are already clashes and protests on the streets which must be dealt with before it gets out of hand."

502.speaker: Orso Hawker
502.text: "You can also justify an action against the Young Sords. After all, they started all this mess with the commies, *and* they killed a man right near the Maroon Palace. That can be considered a declaration of war against the state itself."

503.speaker: Player
503.text: "These Blud separatists have no place in Sordland. They will not be tolerated."

505.speaker: Player
505.text: "I don't want to create problems with our Bludish citizens."

506.speaker: Player
506.text: "There is not enough evidence to connect the separatists with the Worker's party."

507.speaker: Orso Hawker
507.text: "But they are already creating problems for us. Most Bluds in Bergia are either ballsy enough to show their support for the separatists or they vote for the Worker's Party."

508.speaker: Orso Hawker
508.text: "But let's not forget about the socialists."

509.speaker: Orso Hawker
509.text: "Come on, Mr. President. We all know what they stand for. Bluds will be Bluds. They all want to establish their own country in Bergia."

510.speaker: Player
510.text: "Both organizations must be declared as national threats."

512.speaker: Orso Hawker
512.text: "They are an enemy of the state. The state must react."

513.speaker: Orso Hawker
513.text: "They are both enemies of the state."

514.speaker: Orso Hawker
514.text: "I don't think there is much to think."

515.speaker: Orso Hawker
515.text: "But let's talk about how we can deal with them."

516.speaker: Player
516.text: "Sorry to interrupt, Mr. Hawker, but I won't be going ahead with this."

517.speaker: Orso Hawker
517.text: "I thought you wanted to plan our move."

518.speaker: Player
518.text: "I just wanted to hear your plan. And now I've heard it."

520.speaker: Player
520.text: "I thought I wanted to. Instead I will be proceeding with the reforms."

522.speaker: Orso Hawker
522.text: "You will instead push on with your reforms then? It seems you are also part of the conspiracy, after all."

523.speaker: Orso Hawker
523.text: "Is this all a joke to you?"

524.speaker: Orso Hawker
524.text: "It seems you are also part of the conspiracy, after all."

525.speaker: Orso Hawker
525.text: "We should eliminate the threats on our streets first. The police should have the authority to disperse crowds as necessary. We also have to keep the streets clean from the socialist thugs and Bludish separatists."

526.speaker: Orso Hawker
526.text: "We should give more authority to the police regarding their use of force. They should be able to stop and frisk as necessary, especially in Bludish neighbourhoods."

527.speaker: Orso Hawker
527.text: "The police will also need permissions for increased surveillance against these organizations. They should be able to search properties without warrants, and wiretapping should be permissible beyond its current limits."

529.speaker: Player
529.text: "We should suspend the right to protest and disperse the crowds."

530.speaker: Player
530.text: "The police should stop and frisk based on suspicion."

531.speaker: Orso Hawker
531.text: "They will also need to be able to act swiftly. If a person is suspected of crimes against the national security of Sordland, the police should be able to detain them without trial. We cannot allow them proper trials anyway."

534.speaker: Player
534.text: "I think detention without trial is too much."

535.speaker: Orso Hawker
535.text: "We are fighting against national security threats here. These are terrorists. We need extreme measures in extreme situations."

536.speaker: Orso Hawker
536.text: "There are also the external threats we must face."

537.speaker: Orso Hawker
537.text: "And there are also the external threats we must face."

538.speaker: Orso Hawker
538.text: "Rumburg has acted hostile in the past and now they are arming the Bluds. We must cut all ties with them. They need to be embargoed, their citizens must barred from entering Sordland."

539.speaker: Orso Hawker
539.text: "We must erase all of their influence in Sordland, weaken their trade and give them a message."

540.speaker: Player
540.text: "Rumburg is our biggest enemy, we must react."

541.speaker: Player
541.text: "We shouldn't escalate the situation with Rumburg too fast."

542.speaker: Orso Hawker
542.text: "They are the ones who are spitting on us! They already escalated the situation."

543.speaker: Orso Hawker
543.text: "And of course, we need to prepare our army in any case. They have a very powerful military, and they seem to have plans on our soil."

544.speaker: Orso Hawker
544.text: "Then there are the superpowers. Both are influencing our nation to be in their spheres. It seems Arcasia already bought Mr. Ricter and possibly is behind all of this."

545.speaker: Orso Hawker
545.text: "And United Contana is funding Sordish communists against our state. But we cannot bow down to the superpowers. Sordland must stand tall."

547.speaker: Player
547.text: "We will not bow to them, Mr. Hawker."

548.speaker: Orso Hawker
548.text: "I know it is a serious issue. But their actions against our country is obvious. We simply cannot allow them to manipulate us."

549.speaker: Orso Hawker
549.text: "I know we won't. They tried to divide Sordland before, but we came out stronger after the Civil War."

551.speaker: Player
551.text: "We will come out of this stronger again."

552.speaker: Player
552.text: "I agree, but we cannot afford to sever all of our ties with them."

553.speaker: Player
553.text: "We might need one of their support against the other."

554.speaker: Orso Hawker
554.text: "Getting their support means becoming their pawns, Mr. President."

557.speaker: Orso Hawker
557.text: "I do hope so, Mr. President. It will all be up to you."

558.speaker: Narrator
558.text: Orso looked at the clock in the office, and then outside the window.

559.speaker: Orso Hawker
559.text: "Mr. President, I have taken too much of your time already."

560.speaker: Orso Hawker
560.text: "I will be reaching out again after you dissolve the reform committee and end the pursuits for reform."

561.speaker: Player
561.text: "I will stop the reforms shortly. [Proceed with the deal]"

562.speaker: Player
562.text: "I cannot promise you that, Mr. Hawker. We do not have a deal. [Proceed with reforms]"

563.speaker: Orso Hawker
563.text: "Was this all a joke to you?"

564.speaker: Player
564.text: "No, Mr. Hawker. I just wanted to learn about your intentions."

565.speaker: Player
565.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. Hawker. But I won't be doing this."

567.speaker: Narrator
567.text: He looked at me with anger.

568.speaker: Orso Hawker
568.text: "Good luck with your reforms, Mr. President."

570.speaker: Narrator
570.text: He quickly got off the couch and moved towards the door.

572.speaker: Player
572.text: "Don't walk out on me, Mr. Hawker."

577.speaker: Narrator
577.text: He slowly got up from the sofa.

578.speaker: Orso Hawker
578.text: "It was great talking to you. And I am looking forward to our cooperation, Mr. President."

580.speaker: Narrator
580.text: We shook hands on our deal. This also meant that I made an unholy alliance with the Old Guards.

584.speaker: Narrator
584.text: After he left, I called in Lucian and explained to him about my decision to stop the reforms and called Petr to dissolve the committee on the next day.

585.speaker: Narrator
585.text: This was a point of no return.

586.speaker: Heron Garaci
586.text: "Suit yourself, Mr. President. Play into the hands of Sordland's enemies. There will be-"

587.speaker: Orso Hawker
587.text: "Mr. President clearly doesn't want to talk to us. Let's just give him some room before he disrespects the judiciary further."

588.speaker: Narrator
588.text: Orso and Heron both stood up from their seats.

589.speaker: Orso Hawker
589.text: "Please excuse us, Mr. President. Sorry to have taken up your valuable time."

591.speaker: Player
591.text: "I expect your support for the reforms. Don't make a mistake."

597.speaker: Narrator
597.text: Orso and Heron both stood up from their seats.

598.speaker: Heron Garaci
598.text: "Suit yourself, Mr. President. Play into the hands of Sordland's enemies. There will be-"

599.speaker: Narrator
599.text: They both left the room without saying anything else.

600.speaker: Orso Hawker
600.text: "Mr. President clearly doesn't want to talk to us. Let's just give him some room before he disrespects the judiciary further."

603.speaker: Orso Hawker
603.text: "Please excuse us, Mr. President. Sorry to have taken your valuable time."

607.speaker: Player
607.text: "I expect your support for the reforms. Don't make a mistake."

611.speaker: Lucian Galade
611.text: "That was not good. They clearly tried to threaten you."

612.speaker: Player
612.text: "We need to take care of them."

613.speaker: Player
613.text: "We have to make sure our reforms will pass the Court."

614.speaker: Player
614.text: "How dare they talk to me like that?"

615.speaker: Lucian Galade
615.text: "Orso will be doing whatever it takes to damage you."

617.speaker: Lucian Galade
617.text: "We need to be careful. There are still many Old Guard sympathizers in our party. We can't let them divide our party."

619.speaker: Narrator
619.text: After a short evaluation of the situation on our hands, Lucian left me in the presidential office.

620.speaker: Narrator
620.text: It was obvious that the Old Guards would be my main rivals in the near future.

621.speaker: Player
621.text: "There is no conspiracy but yours, Mr. Hawker."

622.speaker: Player
622.text: "I think we should end the meeting before we offend each other."

623.speaker: Player
623.text: "I need to push the reforms, Mr. Hawker, and I will."

625.speaker: Orso Hawker
625.text: "I hope Sordland's future is not bleak."

644.speaker: Player
644.text: "Yes, thank you, Lucian. You can go."

645.speaker: Player
645.text: "Lucian isn't going anywhere. This meeting is over."
